{{Quote|Rebellion is the only option, senator. It's been leading to that ever since the Ghorman Massacre.|Mon Mothma, to Bail Organa|<ref name="The Princess Leia Diaries">{{Tales|11|The Princess Leia Diaries}}</ref>}}
The '''Ghorman Massacre''', also known as the '''Massacre at Ghorman''', was an atrocity perpetrated by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] shortly after [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Declaration of a New Order]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. Following an increase in taxation, [[Ghormanian|citizens]] of the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ghorman/Legends|Ghorman]] staged a peaceful sit-in protest at their [[Ghorman capital square|capital square]] and at landing pads at their [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilfhuff Tarkin]] arrived on Ghorman to collect the taxes and ordered his [[Warship/Legends|warship]] to land on top of the protesters, [[Death/Legends|killing]] and wounding hundreds. Others were also killed and wounded by Imperial [[Troop/Legends|troops]] intervening in the protests.

The massacre horrified many throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and although it initially suppressed resistance to the Empire, it inspired many to openly rebel. [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] decided to support Senator [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma's]] growing [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|resistance movement]] in response to the massacre, having previously rejected the idea of revolution. The massacre was commemorated [[Standard year/Legends|annually]] by Imperial dissenters, and some activists who publicly protested it were forcibly disappeared.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the Republic will be reorganized into the first Galactic Empire! For a safe and secure society!|Palpatine in the Declaration of a New Order|audio=Palpatine-Proclamation.flac|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ghorman.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ghorman, the site of the massacre]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a [[Democracy/Legends|democratic]] institution that had lasted for [[25,053 BBY|25,000 years]], into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], ushering in a [[Imperial Era/Legends|new era]] of totalitarian rule and oppression with himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|emperor]].<ref name="NEC" /> Shortly afterward, the [[Ghormanian]] citizens of [[Ghorman/Legends|Ghorman]], a small planet in the [[Sern sector/Legends|Sern sector]]<ref name="Fact File 31" /> in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> outside of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], loudly expressed their opposition to the new [[Emperor/Legends|emperor]],<ref name="Fact File 31" /> and the [[Ghorman's governor|planetary governor]] of Ghorman refused to bow to Palpatine.<ref name="Technical Journal" /> The Empire levied new taxes on Ghorman; in response,<ref name="NEC" /> thousands of Ghormanians<ref name="Fact File 127">{{FactFile|127|REB 1-2|History of the Rebellion}}</ref> staged a peaceful sit-in protest<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> at the [[Ghorman capital square|capital square]]<ref name="NEC" /> and at the planet's [[Ghorman's primary spaceport|primary spaceport]], blocking the landing pads used by Imperial vessels.<ref name="Technical Journal" />

==The massacre==
{{Quote|Ghorman was the scene of an early massacre, portent of the future of the Empire. A peaceful demonstration against rising taxes turned to tragedy and horror as the Republic warship sent to collect the taxes landed despite the protesters, killing or injuring hundreds.|The pamphlet ''A Call to Reason'', distributed by the Rebel Alliance|<ref name="Farlander">{{StoryCite|story=The Farlander Papers|book=Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)}}</ref>}}
An Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warship]] commanded by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] arrived on Ghorman to collect the taxes.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> Tarkin ordered his [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]<ref name="Fact File 31" /> to land on top of the protestors at the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]],<ref name="Technical Journal" /> [[Death/Legends|killing]] and wounding<ref name="Farlander" /> a majority of the dissenters,<ref name="Fact File 31" /> numbering in the hundreds.<ref name="NEC" /> Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|troops]] also intervened in the protests, killing or wounding hundreds.<ref name="Do No Harm" /> Several members of the [[Republic Group/Legends|Republic Group]], a group of [[Senator/Legends|senators]] who sought to restore the values of the Old Republic, were among the dead.<ref name="Millennium Falcon" /> Those who survived returned to their homes.<ref name="Fact File 31" />

==Aftermath==
===Formation of the Rebellion===
{{Quote|After Ghorman, Bail realized that the Republic was dead. He began to use all of his influence and political skill to aid us, while still pretending to be against me on the floor of the Senate.|Mon Mothma|<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />}}
[[File:Grand_Moff_Tarkin_2015_World_Championship_Prize.png|thumb|left|200px|Wilhuff Tarkin was promoted for his role in the massacre.]]
Across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], many were horrified by the atrocity,<ref name="NEC" /> believing it served as a graphic signal of the end of the Old Republic and their democratic way of life. Ghorman was ultimately one of the first of many worlds to feel Palpatine's [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] wrath.<ref name="Technical Journal" /> The massacre quelled initial unrest across the Empire, pleasing Palpatine.<ref name="Fact File 31" /> Rather than facing prosecution for murdering the Ghormanian protestors, Tarkin was promoted<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> to the role of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]]<ref name="Essential Chronology" /> of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]<ref name="Annual 2008">''[[Star Wars Annual 2008]]''</ref> for his role in crushing the rebellion.<ref name="Whos Who">{{InsiderCite|85|Who's Who in the Delegation of 2000}}</ref> The Empire later established a base on Ghorman.<ref name="SW Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

In the long term, instead of instilling fear,<ref name="Star Wars Rebellion">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] </ref> the Ghorman Massacre became a rallying cry against Imperial oppression,<ref name="Edge of the Empire">[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> serving as a turning point in the growing dissent against the Empire<ref name="Annual 1999">''[[Star Wars Annual 1999]]''</ref> and galvanizing many to openly rebel.<ref name="TFU Guide" /> Ghorman's senator, [[Gebnerret Vibrion]], realized that he and his planet could not remain neutral in response to the Empire's treatment of protestors.<ref name="Do No Harm" /> Senators [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] of the planet [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] of the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] had previously discussed the idea of rebelling against Palpatine, to Organa's initial repulsion, as he instead sought to reform the Empire. The Ghorman Massacre convinced him that the Galactic Republic was dead,<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> and that the Empire's cruelty would only increase, necessitating revolution.<ref name="Fact File 127" /> He began [[Cantham House Meetings|meeting]] with Mothma and Senator [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]]<ref name="Heros Guide">''[[Hero's Guide]]''</ref> secretly<ref name="Essential Chronology" /> and supported Mothma's growing resistance movement through the provision of [[Currency/Legends|funds]], [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]], and information through his positions on the [[Financial Appropriations Committee|Financial Appropriations]] and [[Senate Intelligence Oversight Committee/Legends|Intelligence Oversight Committees]].<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> At one point, Mothma met with the leaders of the [[Corellian Resistance/Legends|Corellian Resistance]] and stated that the Ghorman Massacre, alongside other atrocities on worlds such as [[Rampa 1 uprising|Rampa 1]], [[Rampa 2 uprising|Rampa 2]], and [[Battle of Montellian Serat|Devaron]], demonstrated that Palpatine was either pathologically insane or evil and needed to be removed from power.<ref name="Rebel Dawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> 

[[File:Bail_Organa_and_Mon_Mothma.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Bail Organa (left) and Mon Mothma began working toward the creation of the Alliance to Restore the Republic in response to the Ghorman Massacre.]]
Publicly, Organa continued opposing Mothma in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] until she was forced to [[Mon Mothma's escape from Coruscant|flee]]<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> to escape an arrest warrant from Palpatine.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> During a virtual meeting of the Alliance leadership<ref name="The Princess Leia Diaries" /> around [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="Princess Leia Diaries date">In "[[The Princess Leia Diaries]]," [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] overhears the meeting of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] leadership a [[Standard month/Legends|month]] before turning seventeen. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', places Organa's [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], therefore, she must have overheard the meeting around [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].</ref> Mothma expressed her belief that the Ghorman Massacre had made open rebellion unavoidable.<ref name="The Princess Leia Diaries" /> Later that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Mothma, Organa, and Bel Iblis signed the [[Corellian Treaty]], unifying three large Rebel groups into the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and commencing the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="NEC" /> At a later date, Mothma visited a rebel group on the planet [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]], where she mentioned the Massacre at Ghorman and its role in the formation of the Alliance. The rebellion also produced a pamphlet titled ''[[A Call to Reason]]'', which mentioned the Ghorman Massacre and expressed outrage at the promotion Tarkin received.<ref name="Farlander" /> Senator Vibrion eventually became the leader of a [[Gebnerret Vibrion's resistance group|resistance group]] that joined the Alliance.<ref name="Do No Harm" />

===Remembrance and legacy===
{{Quote|The Empire ruined my life, my parents were political resisters. They marked the anniversary of the Ghorman Massacre, and they protested the destruction of Alderaan—but by that time the Emperor had lost all patience with political objections.|Kyp Durron|<ref name="Dark Apprentice">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>}}
A [[DP20 gunship/Legends|DP20 gunship]] in service to the Alliance was named the ''[[Ghorman's Honor]]'' in tribute to the victims of the massacre.<ref name="Truce at Bakura">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Ghorman Massacre was given its name by members of the Rebellion,<ref name="Tarkin DB">{{DB|character|grandmofftarkin|Tarkin, Grand Moff}}</ref> and its anniversary was commemorated annually by those who opposed the Empire.<ref name="SW Encyclopedia" /> The [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Band/Legends|band]] [[Red Line]] publicly condemned the massacre at a concert, leading to their disappearance by Imperial authorities.<ref name="Slugthrowers">{{SW|url=news/slugthrowers-part-2|series=Slugthrowers: An Overview of Popular Music and Musicians in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> The Ghorman Massacre was considered one of the strongest encapsulations of Imperial cruelty until the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|Destruction of Alderaan]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], also ordered by Tarkin, who would be killed shortly afterward in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:KypDurron_Infobox.png|thumb|left|250px|Kyp Durron and his family were arrested after his parents protested the Ghorman Massacre.]]
On<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> the planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Deyer/Legends|Deyer]], the [[Politics|politician]] [[Kyp Durron's mother|mother]] and [[Kyp Durron's father|father]] of the teenager [[Zeth Durron|Zeth]] and [[Youngling/Legends|child]] [[Kyp Durron]]<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> marked the anniversary of the Ghorman massacre<ref name="Dark Apprentice" /> by protesting.<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Combined with other acts of defiance, the parents' protests led to the arrest of their entire [[Durron family|family]] by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]<ref name="Dark Apprentice" /> in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="1 ABY"> According to ''[[Jedi Search]]'', [[Kyp Durron]] was eight when he and his [[Parent/Legends|parents]] were arrested by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Since he is eighteen in [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']], which was set in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', the [[Durron family]] must have been arrested in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].</ref> Kyp and his parents were sentenced to forced labor in the [[Spice mines of Kessel/Legends|spice mines]]<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> of the planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] while Zeth was sent to the [[Carida Academy|Imperial Academy]] on<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> the planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Carida/Legends|Carida]].<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> The Rebel Alliance was ultimately successful in defeating Palpatine at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], which was followed by the formation of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="NEC" /> Kyp Durron later sought revenge against the Empire, leading to the [[Destruction of Carida|destruction]] of the [[Carida system/Legends|Carida system]]<ref name="NEGTC" /> in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]] and the deaths of billions.<ref name="NEC" />

The Ghorman Massacre was mentioned in ''[[The Essential Chronology]]'', a chronicle of galactic history compiled in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] by the New Republic [[Historical Council]],<ref name="Essential Chronology" /> and in its [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|updated version]] published in [[36 ABY]]. Both editions noted that the event signified that the excesses of the Empire could not be controlled through bureaucratic checks and balances.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Essential Chronology" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Appearances and inspirations===
{{Quote|A large group of people gathered in the Jallianwala Bagh square in Amritsar, Punjab, to protest various British actions, violating a British curfew. Brigadier General R.E.H. Dyer surrounded the enclosed square with Gurkha and Sikh infantry, blocking off all exits, and then ordered the troops to open fire, killing hundreds. This appalling image stuck with me for a very long time.|Paul Murphy, describing the real-world precedent for the Ghorman Massacre|<ref name="Paul Murphy">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/05/08/star-wars/andor-lore-star-wars-rpg-history-ghorman-massacre-paul-murphy-west-end-games|text=The Roots of ‘Andor’ Lore Run Deep|author=Lindbergh, Ben|date=2025-05-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|archivedate=20250609215800}}</ref>}}
[[File:Jallianwala-Bagh-Massacre.jpg|thumb|right|350px|A painting depicting the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which inspired the creation of the Ghorman Massacre]]
The Ghorman Massacre was first mentioned in ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Paul Murphy]] as a supplement to [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' and published in [[1990]].<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> Murphy sought to create an event that would lead those in the Senate to realize the depths of the Empire's cruelty and inspire rebellion. One option he considered was a large scale massacre of [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] to highlight the Empire's bigotry, but he feared the idea would not be accepted by [[Lucasfilm]] and settled on describing a smaller event perpetrated by Wilhuff Tarkin instead. Murphy was inspired by the real-world [[Wikipedia:Jallianwala Bagh massacre|Jallianwala Bagh massacre]] in [[1910s|1919]], in which hundreds of protestors at the [[Wikipedia:Jallianwala Bagh|Jallianwala Bagh]] in [[Wikipedia:Amritsar|Amritsar]] in [[Wikipedia:Punjab, India|Punjab, India]] were surrounded by the [[Wikipedia:British Indian Army|British Indian Army]] and killed.<ref name="Paul Murphy" /> The Ghorman Massacre was later identified as the "massacre at Ghorman" by the [[1993]] novella "[[The Farlander Papers]]" by [[Rusel DeMaria]],<ref name="Farlander" /> and the event was later capitalized as the "Massacre at Ghorman" by the magazine ''[[Star Wars Technical Journal of the Rebel Forces]]'' by [[Lora Johnson]] in the [[1994|following year]].<ref name="Technical Journal" />

===Continuity===
====Inconsistencies====
[[File:TheRebelAllianceSourcebook.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Several discrepancies regarding the Ghorman Massacre have developed since its introduction in ''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook''.]]
There are several conflicting statements across a range of sources regarding details of the massacre. In cases where individual sources conflict with the majority of others, this article follows the events presented in the majority of sources. 

''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook'' stated that dozens of protestors were killed and hundreds wounded,<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> which was reiterated by ''Star Wars Technical Journal of the Rebel Forces''.<ref name="Technical Journal" /> "The Farlander Papers" stated that hundreds were killed or injured,<ref name="Farlander" /> which was repeated in numerous subsequent sources.<ref name="Do No Harm" /><ref name="Essential Chronology" /><ref name="NEGTC" /> However, the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 127|127th issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'',<ref name="Fact File 127" /> written by [[Iain Lowson]]<ref name="FF Author">{{LinkedIn|url=in/iainlowson|text=Iain Lowson}}</ref> published around [[June 2]], [[2004]],<ref name="Fact File 127 Date">{{FactFileDates|127}}</ref> stated that the death toll was in the thousands.<ref name="Fact File 127" />

The magazine ''[[Star Wars Annual 1999]]'', written by [[Dan Whitehead]] and published in [[1998]], states that multiple warships landed on top of the crowds at the spaceport,<ref name="Annual 1999" /> conflicting with other sources that only mention a singular vessel under Tarkin's command.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Technical Journal" /> Beginning with ''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook'', the majority of sources refer to the vessel used in the massacre as a warship.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Technical Journal" /> The [[2002]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] describes the vessel used in the massacre as a collection freighter.<ref name="NEGTC" /> ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', written by [[Jason Fry]] and Wallace and published in [[2009]], refers to the ship as a customs vessel.<ref name="TEA" />

''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook'' placed the massacre at the landing pads at the spaceport on Ghorman,<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> which was repeated by later sources.<ref name="Technical Journal" /><ref name="Annual 1999" /><ref name="Annual 2008" /> ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', a [[2005]] reference book by Wallace and [[Kevin J. Anderson]], stated that the massacre occurred at the capital square instead.<ref name="NEC" />

====Canon adaptation====
{{Quote|There’s also a great dissonance in the canon, because in Legends, they have a ‘Tarkin incident’ 15 years earlier.|Tony Gilroy, on the differing portrayals in Legends and canon of the Ghorman Massacre|<ref name="Tony Gilroy">{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-interview-tony-gilroy|text=Making a Revolutionary: Inside ''Andor'' Season 2 with Tony Gilroy}}</ref>}}
[[File:WHO-StormtroopersCloseIn.png|thumb|right|300px|The canon series ''Andor'' portrayed a massacre (pictured) on Ghorman in 2 BBY while adapting the Legends version as a separate event.]]
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], [[Tony Gilroy]], the showrunner for the [[Disney+]] series [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']], sought to adapt the [[Ghorman Massacre]]<ref name="Tony Gilroy" /> in the [[in-universe]] [[Standard year|year]] [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> while reconciling it with the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] event earlier in the Empire's reign.<ref name="Tony Gilroy" /> "[[Ever Been to Ghorman?]]," written by [[Beau Willimon]]<ref name="Ever been to Ghorman?">{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}}</ref> as the fourth episode of ''Andor''{{'s}} [[Andor Season 2|second season]] which debuted on [[April 29]], [[2025]],<ref name="Trailer News">{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-teaser-trailer-key-art-reveal|text=First ''Andor A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer and Poster Revealed}}</ref> established that [[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] had landed his [[cruiser]] on 500 peaceful protestors in [[Palmo Plaza]] on the [[planet]] [[Ghorman]]<ref name="Ever been to Ghorman?" /> in [[19 BBY]].<ref name="19BBY">"[[Ever Been to Ghorman?]]" dates itself to [[3 BBY]] and establishes the Tarkin Massacre occurred sixteen years prior, putting that event in [[19 BBY]].</ref> Gilroy expressed hope that passionate ''Star Wars'' fans would appreciate the show's synthesis of events on Ghorman.<ref name="Collider Ghorman">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-preview-tony-gilroy-collateral-damage|text=“I Want To Make the Show Timeless”: Tony Gilroy Previews ’Andor Season 2 and the “Collateral Damage” Ahead|author=Maggie Lovitt|date=2025-03-10|archivedate=20250310200653}}</ref> Following the episode's airing, Murphy was interviewed about the role he had played in the portrayal of the Ghorman Massacre, and he expressed both surprise and pride that his initial idea had been adapted for television.<ref name="Paul Murphy" />
